references.text: The contrast between the father's mission that led to his son's disappearance (Gen 37:13) and his prophetic promise that God will gather them again at death (Gen 48:21).
Narrative contrast between the sending that caused the rupture (Gen 37:13) and the reunion that brought restoration (Gen 48:2).
The emotional arc from the father's wish for Joseph to go meet his family (Gen 37:13) to his joy at finally seeing his son's face again (Gen 48:11).
A theological parallel between the call to go to Canaan that triggered the crisis (Gen 37:13) and the promise that God will bring them back there after exile (Gen 50:24).
Narrative inversion: The father sends Joseph down (Gen 37:13), leading to dispersion, while Joseph urges his family to come up (Gen 45:9) to gather them.
The emotional resolution of the father's longing to see Joseph (Gen 37:13) in the expression 'now I can die' because he has seen him again (Gen 46:30).
